record.paper_title: Aspects of Nonabelian Group Based Cryptography: A Survey and Open Problems
record.original_question: For polycyclic-group cryptographic constructions that rely on commuting subgroups, which choice of commuting subgroups makes the schemes secure?

evidence.quote: 9. What is the appropriate choice of commuting subgroups in polycyclic groups which makes the described schemes secure?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a polycyclic group (a group admitting a subnormal series $1 = G_0 \triangleleft G_1 \triangleleft \cdots \triangleleft G_n = G$ with each quotient $G_{i+1}/G_i$ cyclic). Two subgroups $A, B \le G$ are called commuting if $ab = ba$ for every $a \in A$ and $b \in B$ (equivalently, $[A,B] = 1$).

Several non-abelian key-exchange and cryptographic protocols use such a pair $(A,B)$ in $G$ as public data: a public element $g \in G$ is fixed, Alice picks a secret $a \in A$ and publishes $a^{-1} g a$ (or $g^a$), Bob picks a secret $b \in B$ and publishes $b^{-1} g b$, and the shared key $b^{-1} a^{-1} g a b = a^{-1} b^{-1} g b a$ is recoverable by both parties because $A$ and $B$ commute elementwise. The security of such schemes rests on the computational hardness, in $G$, of recovering the secrets from the public transcript (variants of the conjugacy search and commutator key-exchange problems restricted to $A$ and $B$).

Problem: Determine an explicit construction of a polycyclic group $G$ together with a pair of elementwise-commuting subgroups $A, B \le G$ such that the associated key-exchange/commutator protocols above are provably (or at least heuristically) secure against all known attacks — i.e., characterize which choices of commuting subgroup pairs $(A,B)$ in polycyclic platform groups yield secure instances of these schemes.
artifact.status_search_result: A 2016 follow-up survey on the status of polycyclic group-based cryptography (Gryak–Kahrobaei) and a 2022 survey on group-based cryptography in the quantum era (Kahrobaei–Flores) both continue to discuss the choice of commuting subgroups in polycyclic platforms as an unresolved design issue, with no general characterization of secure choices established. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: The Status of Polycyclic Group-Based Cryptography: A Survey and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Survey listing remaining open problems on polycyclic group-based cryptography, including platform/subgroup selection.
status_evidence.claim: The question of how to select commuting subgroups in polycyclic platforms for secure schemes is still listed as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Group-based Cryptography in the Quantum Era
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses commuting-subgroup-based protocols (commutator key-exchange) over polycyclic and other non-abelian platforms and notes ongoing security analysis.
status_evidence.claim: As of 2022, identifying provably secure commuting-subgroup choices in polycyclic groups remains an active open question.
